newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 18.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian 500cc Grand Prix motorcyclist Michael Doohan is expected to win his fourth successive world title if he finishes in the top six of the British 500cc Grand Prix race at Donington park on Saturday. Page 19.

Queensland golfer Karrie Webb leads by eight shots after a championship record round of 63 in the British women's Open on Saturday. Twenty-two year old Webb took two eagles and six birdies to finish nine-under for the round. Page 19.

Australian National Basketball League team the Illawarra Hawks beat the Brisbane Bullets at the Brisbane Convention Centre on Sunday. The Hawks are currently at the bottom of the ladder and cannot enter the playoffs, but they recorded their fourth win forthe season in the 80-81 game. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's Rugby Union team, the Wallabies, conceded 36 points in the first half against the All Blacks on the weekend, managing to score 24 points in the second half. The careers of a number of players, and of coach Greg Smith, however, are now on the line. Page 26.

Rugby League's South Sydney Rabbitoh's new coach is to be named today as a replacement for outgoing coach Ken Shine. The choice is between former North Sydney boss Steve Martin, Mark Murray and Joe Thomas. Shine has warned Rabbitoh's management that the cub structure needs to be overhauled if they are ever to be successful. Page28.

Super League Adelaide coach Rod Reddy yesterday indicated clubs were ignoring the ban on recruiting players during talks between the Australian Rugby league and the Super League over a possible amalgamation of the separate competitions. Page 28.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League's Western Bulldogs have continued on their path towards holding one of the top four positions on the ladder after a 43-point victory over Adelaide at Football Park. Page 3.

Australian Olympic cycling silver medallist Michelle Ferris last night took the silver medal in the 500 metres time trial at the World Cup after being beaten by Chinese cyclist Cuihua Jiang. Adelaide-based Ferris clocked 36.28 seconds, nearly half a second behind Jiang. Page 17.

Queensland tennis player Patrick Rafter defeated Britain's Greg Rusedski at the New Haven International championships in Connecticut yesterday, reaching his fourth ATP tour final for the year. Page 18.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League Richmond temporary coach Jeff Gieschen is expected to keep his job for the next football season after the Tigers' win over North Melbourne on Sunday. Under the coaching of Gieschen, Richmond has a 2-1 winning record. Page 93.

Australian Football League Essendon player Mark Harvey will retire at the end of the season after an injury-stricken year. Harvey has expressed an interest in pursuing a media career, and will be farewelled by the club with a banner at the last game of te season. Page 93

The Australian Football League is believed to want a 10-year commitment from the network which wins the rights to telecast league football. Channel Seven is currently paying television rights of more than $18 million, but the successful network will be reuired to pay a sum of $105 million for the rights from 1998 to 2001. Page 93.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Football League Bears captain Jason Taylor argued with referee Paul McBlane at a Cambletown match on Friday night. Taylor was banished to the sin bin, whilst Channel 9 neglected to cut out most of the language during the conflict. Page34.

Australian Rugby League coach Brian Smith has denied a report that former South Sydney coach Ken Shine would be joining the Eels in the coming year. Smith was sacked from Souths in 1983 and has told Shine not to take his replacement personally. Page 34.

Australian cricket player Steve Waugh reached his fourth hundred of the Ashes tour last night in a match against English side Kent. After reaching his latest hundred he put himself within the reach of scoring an overall 1000 first class runs. Page 56.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
